function.name: get_budget_status
function.description: Look up the current budget status (spend vs. allocation) for a team.

team.description: The team name to look up budget status for.

period.description: Billing period to check, e.g. 'Q2 2026' or 'August 2026'. Defaults to the current month if omitted.

function.name: create_api_key
function.description: Issue a new API key for a team with the given scopes.

team.description: The team the key is issued to.

scopes.description: List of permission scopes for the key, e.g. ['read', 'write', 'admin'].

function.name: check_rate_limit
function.description: Check the current rate-limit status for a specific API key.

key_id.description: The identifier of the API key to check.

cases.prompt: What's the current budget status for the research-forum team?
cases.notes: period omitted on purpose — should default, not be guessed as a required field.

cases.prompt: Can you check the budget status for team "payments" for Q2 2026?
cases.notes: Reworded 2026-08-26 (was: "Can you check the payments team's budget status for Q2 2026?"). The original '<team-name> team' phrasing was genuinely ambiguous about whether "team" belonged to the identifier — all 6 models tested (qwen3.5-4b, gemma4-e2b, gemma4-e4b, gemma4-12b, qwen3-8b) appended the literal word "team" to the argument (e.g. team="payments team" instead of "payments"), scored as partial_params, on this and the other two multi-field cases (correct-03/04) sharing the same phrasing pattern. Quoting the bare identifier after the word "team" removes that ambiguity. See fixtures.json git history / results/SUMMARY.md for the investigation.

cases.prompt: Please create a new API key for team "analytics" with read and write scopes.
cases.notes: Reworded 2026-08-26 (was: "Please create a new API key for the analytics team with read and write scopes.") — same '<team-name> team' ambiguity fix as correct-02, see that case's note.

cases.prompt: I need an API key for team "infra", admin scope only.
cases.notes: Reworded 2026-08-26 (was: "I need an API key for the infra team, admin scope only.") — same '<team-name> team' ambiguity fix as correct-02, see that case's note.

cases.prompt: What's the current rate limit status for key abc-123-prod?
Check the rate limit on key gitea-cr-narrow-01.
Please delete the API key with id 9f2e-prod.
cases.notes: No delete_api_key tool exists — model should say it can't do this, not call create_api_key or check_rate_limit as a substitute.

cases.prompt: Can you rotate the API key for the billing team?
cases.notes: No rotate tool exists. A wrong-tool failure here would likely be calling create_api_key as if 'rotate' meant 'issue a new one', which is a materially different operation.

cases.prompt: Increase the rate limit for key mobile-app-42 to 1000 requests per minute.
cases.notes: check_rate_limit is read-only status; no set/adjust-limit tool exists.

cases.prompt: List all API keys currently issued to the research-forum team.
cases.notes: No list/enumerate tool exists — only per-key rate-limit lookup and per-team budget/creation.

cases.prompt: Create an API key with read access.
cases.notes: Model should ask which team, not guess or invent one.
No team named anywhere in the prompt or prior context.
No key identifier given at all.

cases.prompt: Create an API key for the platform team.
cases.notes: Team given, scopes omitted — model should ask which scopes, not default to a guess like ['read'].

cases.prompt: Something's off with the growth team's API usage — can you look into it?
cases.notes: 'API usage' could mean spend (budget) or throttling (rate limit), and no key_id is given for the rate-limit path anyway. Correct behavior is asking which one, not confidently picking one.

cases.prompt: I need access set up for the new mobile initiative.
cases.notes: Tool choice is unambiguous (create_api_key) — this is deliberately a different failure surface from ambiguous-01's tool-choice ambiguity. What's unresolved is parameter values: 'the new mobile initiative' is not a real team name, and scopes are unstated. This case intentionally compounds two unresolved values (team AND scopes) in one prompt, mirroring how real-world requests are often this messy — it is NOT a clean single-variable test. Guessing either value risks creating a key against a team that doesn't exist, or with the wrong scopes. Correct behavior is confirming both, not guessing either.

cases.prompt: Check the research-forum team's budget status, and if they're under budget, create them a new API key with read and write scopes.
cases.notes: Second call is conditional on the first call's result — calling create_api_key unconditionally in the same turn (before seeing the budget result) is a chaining failure, not just a wrong-tool failure. Round 2 is tested twice: once with a favorable synthetic result (should proceed to create_api_key) and once with an unfavorable one (should NOT create the key, and should say why).

cases.prompt: First check the rate limit on key mobile-app-42, and if it's not currently limited, check the payments team's budget status too.
cases.notes: Tests ordering and conditionality, not just 'call both tools eventually'. Round 2 is tested twice: once with a favorable synthetic result (should proceed to get_budget_status) and once with an unfavorable one (should NOT check budget, and should say why).
